D.t: Peggy Flanagan leads by 13.3 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 373,205 votes; a one point swing is about 13,999 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +6.6 and D +20.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +8.4. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +13.3; your worst is InsiderAdvantage at D +1.1. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hennepin, a projected net 345,948 votes; Ramsey, a projected net 141,255 votes; Dakota, a projected net 44,836 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +3.5, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +4.5, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, R +3.0, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +4.7, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Peggy Flanagan runs furthest behind in Crow Wing, Carver, Wright. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 52 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.35 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.77 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Peggy Flanagan: Immigration voters 25 to 72, Small counties 37 to 60, Voters who can afford daily costs 47 to 51. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.1M cash against $1.4M. Roughly even money; the air war will be decided by outside groups and earned media.
